context: Accessibility demonstration — a dual-panel grouped bar chart showing the same quarterly revenue data under normal vision and a deuteranopia simulation, with bars dual-encoded via color and texture pattern
first_impression: Clean, purposeful layout with a clear conceptual argument, but the charts occupy only the top half of the viewport leaving conspicuous dead space below.
what_works: The Tol Bright palette choice is deliberate and genuinely colorblind-safe; the side-by-side deuteranopia filter panel concretely validates the technique rather than just asserting it works. Axis styling is restrained — no domain lines, light dashed gridlines — and the pattern vocabulary (hatch, horizontal, stipple, crosshatch) is sufficiently distinct.
what_doesnt: The bottom 35-40% of the rendered viewport is empty, giving the layout an unfinished, undersized feel — the charts should either be taller or the container should be sized to content. The legend labels are verbose ('Electronics (diagonal hatch)') and partially redundant once the patterns are visible in the bars, adding textual clutter that competes with the subtitle.
